guide.title: Grammar Lesson Guide
guide.intro: Welcome to the Grammar Roadmap from A to Z!
guide.intro2: You will learn each topic step by step, from basic to advanced.
guide.step1: Read the guide - Understand grammar structures and usage through clear examples
guide.step2: Read & remember - Move through small sections to understand the lesson more deeply
guide.step3: Study examples - Compare correct patterns and common mistakes
guide.step4: Practice several times - The more you practice, the longer the structures stay with you
guide.step5: Take a short quiz - Unlock the next lesson
guide.currentIcon: Current lesson - Study now to unlock the next lesson!
guide.lockedIcon: Locked - Complete the current lesson to continue
guide.tipText: Practice each lesson at least 3-5 times until you understand the structure well, then move to the next lesson.
guide.closing: Stay consistent for 10-15 minutes a day, and grammar will become much easier to understand!

guide.title: Grammar Exercise Guide
guide.intro: Choose the grammar exercise you want to practice from the list.
guide.description: Each exercise includes grammar questions such as multiple choice, fill in the blank, and translation.
guide.multipleChoice: Multiple Choice: Choose the best answer from the given options.
guide.fillBlank: Fill in the Blank: Enter the correct word to complete the sentence.
guide.translation: Translation: Translate the sentence from Vietnamese to English or the other way around.
guide.noteCheck: Press Check after answering each question to view the answer and explanation.

guide.noteSubmit: Press Submit and the system will show your result, including total questions, correct answers, incorrect answers, and accuracy. Press View history to review what you answered and see where you were right or wrong.

guide.title: Pronunciation Lesson Guide
guide.intro: Welcome to the Pronunciation Roadmap from A to Z! You will learn each sound step by step, from basic to advanced.
guide.step1: Watch the guide – Observe mouth, tongue, and airflow placement from a native-style model
guide.step2: Listen & repeat – Listen to each sentence and practice speaking accurately
guide.step3: Compare your voice with native speech – The system scores similarity from 0–100
guide.step4: Practice many times – More practice means better scores and more natural pronunciation
guide.step5: Take a short quiz – Unlock the next lesson after completing it
guide.currentIcon: Current lesson – Start now to unlock the next lesson!
guide.lockedIcon: Locked – Complete the current lesson to continue
guide.tipText: Practice each lesson at least 3–5 times until you reach a 90+ native-like score before moving on.
guide.closing: Stay consistent for 10–15 minutes a day and your pronunciation will become much more natural!

graph.title: How Flashcard Review Contributions Are Counted
graph.intro: The contribution graph shows your flashcard review history over the past 52 weeks. Each square represents one day, and the color shows how many times you rated flashcard difficulty on that day.
graph.rule1: Each time you choose "Easy", "Normal", or "Hard" for a flashcard in a list you created, the system records 1 review for that day.
graph.rule2: Only reviews of your own flashcards count (in the "For you" tab). Reviews of other people's flashcards (in the "Explore" tab) are not counted.
graph.rule3: Square colors are based on the number of reviews compared with the highest-review day in the displayed range:
graph.colorHigh: Closer to the maximum: darker green
graph.colorExample: Example: if the highest day has 100 reviews, then 100 = darkest green, 50 = medium green, and lower values fade gradually.
graph.note1: The graph updates daily using the Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh timezone.
graph.note2: Weeks start on Monday and end on Sunday.
graph.note3: Month labels help you navigate time. Colors are relative to the current data.
graph.closing: Keep your review habit going and your graph will get greener!
